## Project Overview

`class-validator` is a TypeScript validation library for class properties, supporting both decorator-based and non-decorator validation [package.json][README.md:1-11]. It uses `validator.js` internally and supports both Node.js and browser environments [README.md:7-11]. The package is version `0.15.1` and is licensed under MIT [package.json][LICENSE:2-4].

The public API’s likely main entry point is `src/index.ts`, which exposes asynchronous `validate`, rejecting `validateOrReject`, synchronous `validateSync`, and schema registration functions [src/index.ts:46-60][src/index.ts:79-96][src/index.ts:121-142]. The main implementation technologies are TypeScript, Node.js, `validator`, and `libphonenumber-js` [package-lock.json:1-45]. Rollup and the TypeScript compiler produce CommonJS, ES2015, ES5 module, UMD, and declaration outputs [package.json][tsconfig.prod.cjs.json][tsconfig.prod.esm2015.json][tsconfig.prod.esm5.json][tsconfig.prod.types.json].

The library’s validation model stores decorator metadata, resolves custom constraints through a container, and executes synchronous, asynchronous, conditional, nested, promise, group, and whitelist validation [src/metadata/MetadataStorage.ts:10-157][src/container.ts:39-59][src/validation/ValidationExecutor.ts:39-117][src/validation/ValidationExecutor.ts:170-217]. Consumer-facing usage normally begins by importing validators and validation functions from `class-validator`, applying decorators to class properties, instantiating the class, and calling `validate` or `validateOrReject` [README.md:53-121].

## Setup / Installation

Node.js and npm are prerequisites because the repository’s CI installs Node.js and runs npm commands [ .github/workflows/continuous-integration-workflow.yml:6-13]. The package lock records TypeScript `5.4.5`, whose declared engine requires Node.js `>=14.17`, but the evidence does not provide one repository-wide Node.js version requirement [package-lock.json:6280-6292]. CI tests against both the current Node.js release and the current LTS release [ .github/workflows/continuous-integration-workflow.yml:14-27].

npm is the visible package manager: the repository contains a version-2 `package-lock.json`, Dependabot uses the npm ecosystem, and CI uses `npm ci --ignore-scripts` [package-lock.json:1-5][.github/dependabot.yml:1-6][.github/workflows/continuous-integration-workflow.yml:6-13]. For a repository checkout, install the locked dependencies with:

```sh
npm ci --ignore-scripts
```

This is the installation command used by the CI, build, and release workflows [ .github/workflows/continuous-integration-workflow.yml:6-13][.github/workflows/continuous-integration-workflow.yml:20-27][.github/workflows/continuous-deployment-workflow.yml:8-15].

For installation as a dependency in another project, use:

```sh
npm install class-validator --save
```

The consumer documentation requires at least npm 6 because it relies on a flattened dependency tree [README.md:45-52]. A prerelease can instead be installed with `npm install --save class-validator@next`, although the documentation warns that this version may break without notice and should not be used in production [docs/introduction/installation.md:13-21].

Runtime dependencies are `@types/validator`, `libphonenumber-js`, and `validator` [package.json]. Development dependencies include TypeScript, Jest, `ts-jest`, Rollup, ESLint, Prettier, `ts-node`, Husky, and `lint-staged` [package.json].

No local runtime environment variables are documented in the supplied setup evidence; `.env` is merely ignored by Git [.gitignore]. CI and deployment use repository secrets such as `CODECOV_TOKEN`, `NPM_PUBLISH_TOKEN`, and `TYPESTACK_BOT_TOKEN`, but these are workflow credentials rather than documented local configuration [ .github/workflows/continuous-integration-workflow.yml:28-37][.github/workflows/continuous-deployment-workflow.yml:24-29][.github/workflows/auto-approve-dependabot-workflow.yml:7-17].

## Running Locally

The evidence does not show a development server, `start` script, or watch-mode application command; this appears to be a library rather than a hosted application [package.json][README.md:7-11]. No local network port is shown in the supplied repository evidence [package.json][.github/workflows/continuous-integration-workflow.yml:1-52].

A practical local validation workflow is to run formatting, linting, tests, and then the desired build target using the repository scripts [package.json]:

```sh
npm run prettier:check
npm run lint:check
npm run test:ci
npm run build
```

The default `build` script invokes `build:cjs`, while `build:clean` removes the `build` directory [package.json]. The available build targets are:

```sh
npm run build:es2015
npm run build:esm5
npm run build:cjs
npm run build:umd
npm run build:types
```

These compile ES2015 modules, ES5-targeted modules, CommonJS modules, a Rollup UMD bundle, and TypeScript declarations respectively [package.json][tsconfig.prod.esm2015.json][tsconfig.prod.esm5.json][tsconfig.prod.cjs.json][tsconfig.prod.types.json]. CI runs every listed build target after installing dependencies [ .github/workflows/continuous-integration-workflow.yml:38-52].

Formatting can be checked with `npm run prettier:check` or rewritten with `npm run prettier:fix` [package.json]. TypeScript source can be checked with `npm run lint:check` or automatically fixed with `npm run lint:fix`; both lint the `src/` tree [package.json]. Jest watch mode is available through `npm run test:watch` [package.json].

For quick experimentation, the repository documents examples under `sample/`, including basic decorators, validation groups, nested objects, custom validators, custom decorators, inheritance, maps, and sets [README.md:970-974][sample/sample1-simple-validation/Post.ts:20-49][sample/sample2-using-groups/Post.ts:3-36][sample/sample3-nested-objects/Post.ts:4-12][sample/sample4-custom-validator/Post.ts:17-22][sample/sample6-custom-decorator/User.ts:4-14][sample/sample7-inheritance-support/Post.ts:4-14][sample/sample8-es6-maps/Post.ts:4-12][sample/sample9-es6-sets/Post.ts:4-12].

## Project Structure

- `src/index.ts` is the likely public API boundary for top-level validation functions [src/index.ts:46-60][src/index.ts:79-96][src/index.ts:121-142].
- `src/decorator/` contains validation decorators and their underlying predicate functions, divided into categories such as `array`, `common`, `date`, `number`, `object`, `string`, and `typechecker` [src/decorator/array/ArrayContains.ts:10-35][src/decorator/common/ValidateBy.ts:6-34][src/decorator/date/MaxDate.ts:9-31][src/decorator/number/Min.ts:9-31][src/decorator/object/IsInstance.ts:9-39][src/decorator/string/IsEmail.ts:12-35][src/decorator/typechecker/IsString.ts:9-27].
- `src/decorator/ValidationOptions.ts` defines decorator-level options including per-item validation, custom messages, groups, unconditional execution, context, and conditional `validateIf` callbacks [src/decorator/ValidationOptions.ts:6-37].
- `src/metadata/` stores validation and custom-constraint metadata, groups metadata by property, and resolves inherited metadata [src/metadata/ValidationMetadata.ts:7-98][src/metadata/ConstraintMetadata.ts:7-47][src/metadata/MetadataStorage.ts:63-149].
- `src/validation/` contains the core validator, execution engine, validation options, error representation, message-token replacement, and custom-constraint interface [src/validation/Validator.ts:9-113][src/validation/ValidationExecutor.ts:15-437][src/validation/ValidatorOptions.ts:4-89][src/validation/ValidationError.ts:4-94][src/validation/ValidationUtils.ts:18-51][src/validation/ValidatorConstraintInterface.ts:5-15].
- `src/validation-schema/` contains schema types and transformation into internal metadata, although the README states that schema-based validation is no longer supported and has been broken since version `0.12` [src/validation-schema/ValidationSchema.ts:5-65][src/validation-schema/ValidationSchemaToMetadataTransformer.ts:9-34][README.md:962-965].
- `src/container.ts` provides a default object container and optional integration with a user-supplied inversion-of-control container [src/container.ts:22-30][src/container.ts:39-59].
- `src/register-decorator.ts` is the registration boundary for custom decorators and adapts inline validators into constraint metadata [src/register-decorator.ts:11-46][src/register-decorator.ts:51-87].
- `src/utils/` contains shared utilities for converting arrays, sets, and maps; detecting promises; and finding the global object across runtimes [src/utils/convert-to-array.util.ts:4-9][src/utils/is-promise.util.ts:3-5][src/utils/get-global.util.ts:7-31].
- `test/functional/` contains broader behavioral tests, while some unit specifications are colocated with implementations under `src/` [test/functional/conditional-validation.spec.ts:6-95][test/functional/nested-validation.spec.ts:7-335][src/decorator/common/IsIn.spec.ts:3-17][src/decorator/string/IsPhoneNumber.spec.ts:3-43].
- `sample/` contains focused usage examples for major features [sample/sample1-simple-validation/Post.ts:20-49][sample/sample4-custom-validator/CustomTextLength.ts:5-9][sample/sample6-custom-decorator/IsLongerThan.ts:7-26].
- `docs/` is organized into introduction, basics, advanced usage, decorator reference, recipes, and API reference, and GitBook is configured to use `docs` as its root [docs/README.md:1-38][.gitbook.yaml:1-4].
- Root-level configuration includes TypeScript build configurations, Jest configuration, ESLint configuration, Prettier configuration, Codecov configuration, and GitHub Actions workflows [tsconfig.json][tsconfig.spec.json][jest.config.js][.eslintrc.yml][.prettierrc.yml][codecov.yml:1-14][.github/workflows/continuous-integration-workflow.yml:1-52].

## Testing

The repository uses Jest `29.7.0` with `ts-jest` for TypeScript tests and the Node test environment [package-lock.json:1-45][jest.config.js]. Jest compiles tests using `tsconfig.spec.json` [jest.config.js][tsconfig.spec.json].

The available test commands are:

```sh
npm test
npm run test:watch
npm run test:ci
```

`npm test` runs Jest with coverage and verbose output, `test:watch` runs Jest in watch mode, and `test:ci` runs tests serially with no cache, coverage, and verbose output [package.json]. CI runs `npm run test:ci` against Node.js LTS and current releases [ .github/workflows/continuous-integration-workflow.yml:14-27].

Coverage collection targets `src/**/*.ts` while excluding barrel `index.ts` files and interface files [jest.config.js]. Codecov applies coverage status to `src/**/*.ts`, ignores `testing/**/*.ts` and `src/**/*.interface.ts`, and CI uploads `coverage/clover.xml` plus `coverage/lcov-report/` [codecov.yml:1-14][.github/workflows/continuous-integration-workflow.yml:28-37].

Tests are found both in `test/`, including `test/functional/*.spec.ts` and `test/utils.spec.ts`, and beside implementations under `src/` as files such as `IsIn.spec.ts` and `IsPhoneNumber.spec.ts` [test/functional/conditional-validation.spec.ts:6-95][test/utils.spec.ts:3-33][src/decorator/common/IsIn.spec.ts:3-17][src/decorator/string/IsPhoneNumber.spec.ts:3-43]. The supplied evidence does not show a dedicated Jest setup file, and `jest.config.js` does not declare one [jest.config.js].

Visible tests use Jest’s `describe`, `it`, `beforeEach`, `expect`, and `expect.assertions` patterns [test/functional/reject-validation.spec.ts:12-39]. Asynchronous behavior is tested by returning validation promises or using `async`/`await`, while synchronous behavior is exercised through `validateSync` [test/functional/conditional-validation.spec.ts:7-20][test/functional/validation-error.spec.ts:14-89][test/functional/sync-validation.spec.ts:50-69]. The functional suite covers conditional validation, custom decorators and constraints, inherited rules, nested arrays/sets/maps, promises, rejecting validation, error rendering, validator options, and whitelisting [test/functional/conditional-validation.spec.ts:6-95][test/functional/custom-decorators.spec.ts:10-106][test/functional/inherited-validation.spec.ts:6-37][test/functional/nested-validation.spec.ts:7-335][test/functional/promise-validation.spec.ts:7-155][test/functional/reject-validation.spec.ts:12-39][test/functional/validation-error.spec.ts:13-90][test/functional/validator-options.spec.ts:6-86][test/functional/whitelist-validation.spec.ts:7-75].
